tagline: The old coast-to-coast road, from Ruston to the Mississippi.
intro: Before the interstates, US 80 ran clear across the country, and much of it had been the auto trail called the Dixie Overland Highway. In north Louisiana the state keeps 105 miles of it as a byway, from Ruston east by Monroe and Tallulah to the Mississippi River opposite Vicksburg. I-20 runs alongside now and carries the long-distance traffic.
The road crosses farm and timber country and is still a working route for farmers and loggers. Ruston, where it starts, is known for its peaches and has an 18-block historic district.

moments.title: Biedenharn Museum and Gardens
moments.text: Joseph Biedenharn, credited with first bottling Coca-Cola, built this house beside the Ouachita in 1913, then with his son bought a crop-dusting business that grew into Delta Air Lines.

moments.title: Poverty Point
moments.text: Just outside Delhi, six concentric C-shaped earthen ridges, raised in the Late Archaic period and found nowhere else, run out to the edge of Macon Ridge.

moments.title: Delta
moments.text: Across the river from Vicksburg, Delta is the birthplace of Madam C. J. Walker and keeps a remnant of Grant's Canal, dug in 1862 and 1863 to get around the Confederate guns.
